messages.subject: Re: Figuring out which file each record comes from (and other environment variables)
parts:
On Monday, June 11, 2012 10:55:59 AM UTC-7, Saar wrote:
I'm looking for a way to access environment variables from within the mapper. Specifically, the file name that is being read

Sys.getenv("map_input_file"). 
 
and the 'mapper identity' (some kind of ID that would be different for different mappers). 

Sys.getenv("mapred_task_id") or something of this sort (the documentation is a little confusing on this). As I told you in the past, I suspect this could have  few legitimate uses and many counterproductive ones, so if you are willing to share what the original problem was we may find a different solution or I am going to learn something new. Remember tasks can be attempted multiple times, potentially in parallel. Those are different processes. To get a full list of available env variables to a task attempt  try 


```
from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(1), map = function(k,v) keyval(NULL, Sys.getenv())))[[1]]$val
```
 
I don't see how to implement this portably across backends, so it's highly discouraged for that reason alone. "A man warned is half saved".


Antonio


What would be a good way of doing that?
In my specific application knowing just the 'basename' would be enough - I don't need a full path name. For the mapper ID, any ID that would be unique to each mapper process will be sufficient. 

Thanks, 

-Saar

messages.author: 9d5783260b3a4880
messages.subject: Re: Figuring out which file each record comes from (and other environment variables)
parts:
The input file name is needed for two cases (so far):
- Creating some form of a 'document term matrix' when I have multiple documents (with different names) in one folder, and I want to go over all of them and know which word came from which file
- I have a couple of different types of data that I need to work with, and the easiest way to figure out how to interpret a row of data is to know which file it came from. I know that in a perfect world I'd just change the way data is being saved, but my world isn't perfect. 

The reason why I'd want to use some process ID is to convert data from a 'matrix' format (a comma separated file) to a triplet format (rowID, columnID, value). I need to generate some form of a unique rowID for examples such as the linear least squares regression in the tutorial on the Rhadoop wiki. In this case I just need unique rowIDs, not necessarily consecutive rowIDs, so a combination of mapperID and an ongoing row count can be used as a unique rowID. 

I don't think I should worry too much about more than one mapper working on the same line of code, as long as hadoop makes sure that only the outputs from one such mappers actually goes on to be reduced. If I should worry about more than one output from the same row being processed by multiple possible mappers being passed on to the reduce phase, my worries would be too worrisome to handle: in such a case the basic word count example is prone to produce wrong results. 

It would be interesting to find an alternative way to transform data from a comma-separated matrix-like form to a triplet from (rowID, columnID, value) without resorting to crude measures like mapper ID and an ongoing row counter - let me know if you have one. 

-Saar

On Mon, Jun 11, 2012 at 12:56 PM, Saar <sa...@revolutionanalytics.com> wrote:
The input file name is needed for two cases (so far):
- Creating some form of a 'document term matrix' when I have multiple documents (with different names) in one folder, and I want to go over all of them and know which word came from which file
- I have a couple of different types of data that I need to work with, and the easiest way to figure out how to interpret a row of data is to know which file it came from. I know that in a perfect world I'd just change the way data is being saved, but my world isn't perfect.
This looks like a perfectly reasonable application to me. In fact it would be easy to support it even in local mode, it's just that the information is not available to the user and this can be fixed.

The reason why I'd want to use some process ID is to convert data from a 'matrix' format (a comma separated file) to a triplet format (rowID, columnID, value). I need to generate some form of a unique rowID for examples such as the linear least squares regression in the tutorial on the Rhadoop wiki.

You could try something like this:

```
mapmake = function(){count = 0; function(k,v) {count <<- count + 1; keyval(c(Sys.getenv("mapred_task_id",count),v)}}
```

And then run

```
out  = mapreduce(input, map = mapmake())
 ```

Not sure it's a great solution, but I don't see an easy alternative. By sheer luck, this could work in local mode as well, as the env variable is unset but there is a single mapper process, so it doesn't matter.

Antonio

If I should worry about more than one output from the same row being processed by multiple possible mappers being passed on to the reduce phase, my worries would be too worrisome to handle: in such a case the basic word count example is prone to produce wrong results. 

It would be interesting to find an alternative way to transform data from a comma-separated matrix-like form to a triplet from (rowID, columnID, value) without resorting to crude measures like mapper ID and an ongoing row counter - let me know if you have one. 

-Saar
